data.description: This risk factor flags entities identified as Chinese State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) based on established patterns in Chinese-language corporate naming conventions. Entities are included where company names begin with "中国" (China) or "中华" (Chinese), reference the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission ("国务院国资委" or "国有资产监督管理委员会"), or include the term "国企" (state-owned enterprise) alongside other characters. These naming elements are formally associated with state ownership and oversight in China, providing a reliable basis for SOE classification.

data.description: This entity has a "High Risk" ESG Controversy Exposure Score (61-80). Scores are derived from three primary components -- intensity scores, volume scores, and novelty scores. The intensity score measures the severity of each identified ESG incident involving the company, considering its impact on an entity's reputation, stakeholders, financial standing, and legal implications. The volume score assesses the number of articles associated with each event within a short-term rolling window. To ensure accuracy, the volume score is normalized against the average article volume concerning the company and relevant ESG topics over the past year, reducing potential bias. The novelty score accounts for how recent a topic is, weighing them accordingly. News and events related to old topics are discounted, while new topics are assigned heavier weights for a given entity. To see the events that contributed to this score, including ESG subcategory, intensity, and article summaries, please see the associated adverse media records.

data.description: This entity may have directly exported to Russia, Belarus, or Iran one or more shipments with Harmonized System (HS) codes corresponding to critical U.S. components that Russia relies on for its weapons systems. These HS codes listed in Tier 1 and Tier 2 of the U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security's Common High Priority List (CHPL) are subject to the most comprehensive controls under the Export Administration Regulations (15 CFR Parts 730 – 774) (EAR), meaning a license is required for items associated with these HS codes destined for these jurisdictions, including certain foreign-produced items. data.description: This entity may have directly exported to Russia, Belarus, or Iran one or more shipments with Harmonized System (HS) codes corresponding to critical U.S. components that Russia relies on for its weapons systems. These HS codes listed in Tier 1 and Tier 2 of the U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security's Common High Priority List (CHPL) are subject to the most comprehensive controls under the Export Administration Regulations (15 CFR Parts 730 – 774) (EAR), meaning a license is required for items associated with these HS codes destined for these jurisdictions, including certain foreign-produced items.
